findings.summary: The named root cause is false: the base brief already resolved cited job ids to their recorded deliverables and showed them to the reader.
findings.evidence: At base, carry() in crates/athena-core/src/reading/retry.rs:784-823 already fills reading_deliverables for every referenced job. prior_result_section chains inputs.referenced_jobs and prints 'Allowed change scope, deliverables:' with each one. The base test a_follow_up_brief_carries_the_result_and_scope_of_each_named_job asserts '> modify README.md' for a referenced job. The failing job's own reading shows the reader saw that data (evidence records/jobs/2026-11/20261109-075120-7zqw/reading-1.json): it lists the cited jobs' deliverables ('docs/decisions.md, athena.toml, ci.yml, xtask, ...') and says 'neither left a candidate to keep or drop'. It still wrote 'zaj2 (12 deliverables)', while the introspection says the record has 11. So the doc comment and the CHANGELOG describe a gap that did not exist. The gap that actually caused the failure is not fixed: nothing made the rule's thresholds and fixtures come from the records (introspection yxah's prevention). Simpler, more correct alternatives: add the deliverable count, and the summary and criteria if wanted, to the existing per-job entry in prior_result_section. Or fix the place the shape was invented (the criteria and producer side: fixtures loaded from recorded shapes).

summary: This change should not land: it is aimed at the wrong root cause, so it would not prevent this failure class. It adds a recorded reading summary, criteria and deliverables, each with a count, to the reader brief's "Referenced jobs" section, plus one line telling the reader to take sizes, thresholds and fixtures from those deliverables. The new tests pass: I ran `cargo test -p athena-context referenced` (5 passed) and `cargo test -p athena-context` (134 passed), and Athena's recorded fmt, clippy and test checks passed. But the cause it names, in both the doc comment and CHANGELOG.md, is wrong. The base brief already showed every cited job's recorded deliverables in its "Previous result and change scope" section, and an existing base test asserts this. The failing job's reading (7zqw, read from the evidence snapshot) shows its reader saw them and still miscounted one job's deliverables as 12; the record has 11. So the real gap is still open: nothing made the rule's thresholds and test fixtures come from the recorded shapes. The change also prints each cited job's deliverable list a second time, against the intent of criterion 4. Its test does not cover the retried-job or followed-up cases, so I count criterion 4 as unmet. The second instance of the class (job fzx0) is not addressed at all. Verdict: fail, on two major findings and criterion 4.
